title: NRP cleared in death of man in holding cell
article: The province's civilian police watchdog has exonerated the Niagara Regional Police from criminal responsibility in connection with the death of a man in a St. Catharines holding cell last October.
The Special Investigations Unit released the finding Tuesday, saying the moderate force used to arrest Andrew Campbell, 21, in connection with a Pine Street North variety store robbery was lawful.
Reports from Oct. 10, 2005 show Campbell, originally from Big Bras d'Or, Nova Scotia, and a friend walked into Lucky's Video.

A source inside the store at the time told This Week Campbell and his friend came in around 1 p.m. Her husband, who was serving another customer, noticed Campbell put an ice cream bar and candy into his pocket without paying.

Her husband tried to tell Campbell to pay for the goods but was ignored. Campbell and his acquaintance, who were recognized by the owners as regular customers, left the store. The owner followed and was punched in the head repeatedly when he confronted Campbell outside. The source said Campbell threw the candy at her husband, who fell to the ground and was kicked.
After the NRP were called and tipped off to a St. David's Road East home, officers entered and tried to arrest Campbell for robbery.
An angry Campbell reportedly put up a mild struggle with two officers but calmed down while in a squad car and was transported to the St. Catharines station house, arriving just before 3 p.m.
The SIU report says while at the station, Campbell spoke clearly and walked without help and none of the NRP officers who had contact with him suspected he was drunk or high on drugs.
One officer did note Campbell appeared groggy.

As police ran through the booking procedure, asking questions about his health, photographing and fingerprinting him, none of the responses Campbell offered gave officers any cause for concern about his well-being.

Campbell was locked up at around 3:45 p.m. for an overnight stay. During that time, officers checked the cell about every half-hour and found him to be sleeping each time. Just before 7:30 the next morning, an officer serving breakfast couldn't get a response from Campbell. CPR was administered until paramedics arrived. Campbell was then taken to hospital where he was pronounced dead.
Autopsy and toxicology reports revealed Campbell had taken a lethal amount of drugs in the hours before his arrest.
In a release, SIU director David Cornish officially cleared the NRP in the case.
"There is no evidence that any act or omission on the part of any police officer caused or contributed to the tragic and untimely death of Mr. Campbell," said Cornish.
Fifteen police and civilian witnesses were interviewed by the SIU.
While Campbell may be known in Niagara in connection with the case, that isn't the whole story of his life.

He was awarded a Governor-General's medal of bravery for heroism in 2003 for saving the lives of his 14-year-old brother and two other boys from drowning off the shores of a Nova Scotia beach a year earlier. While swimming during a family camping trip, he and his brother were caught in an undertow. Grabbing a body board, Campbell swam back to his brother, pulled him to shallower waters and upon hearing other cries for help, swam back out and saved two younger boys who were being pulled further out to sea.
